free_tier.stated: free subdomain registration under EU.org; no page read states a renewal rule or a renewal fee

per_object_cap.stated: no record count is published; the cap is the review, not a number

retention.stated: unverified: the home, registration, general policy and direct-subdomain policy pages state no term, expiry or renewal rule

interface_detail: no API is documented: the contact and the domain request go through the web form at https://nic.eu.org/arf/; EU.org publishes only the NS delegation, so record management and any dynamic update are those of the DNS host the delegation names
tooling: the nic.eu.org web form, then your own DNS provider
chaining: a free domain that can be a Cloudflare zone, which is the only free option in this set that can

limits.value: every registration needs a human to validate it and 'can take a few days'; no approval rate and no queue length is published

identity_cost.detail: a contact with a name, an e-mail address (the form warns that Gmail addresses cannot receive the validation e-mail), a postal address of at least two lines and a country, with phone and fax optional; then a domain request whose nameservers already serve the zone, validated by a person in what the registration page calls a few days; no card (https://nic.eu.org/arf/en/contact/create/, https://nic.eu.org/register.html)

reliability_note: the operator is a volunteer organisation and the review queue is the service
confidence_note: the home, registration, general policy, direct-subdomain policy and contact-creation pages were read and quoted; they give the review time as a few days and state no renewal rule

evidence.proved: the six-step registration process, whose step 6 is 'Wait for an e-mail reply indicating that your request has been validated. This step requires human intervention and can take a few days.'
the general policy: small commercial sites are accepted but 'VERY STRONGLY' asked to reserve a domain at an ICANN-accredited registrar instead
registration is free; the home page says nothing of renewal
evidence.quote: The main goal of EU.org is to provide free subdomain registration to users or non-profit organizations who cannot afford the fees demanded by some NICs.

evidence.proved: every request is validated by a person, in what the page calls a few days; the registration steps state no term and no renewal
evidence.quote: Wait for an e-mail reply indicating that your request has been validated. This step requires human intervention and can take a few days.

evidence.proved: a Gmail address cannot receive the contact validation e-mail
evidence.quote: Don't use Gmail addresses here, you will not be able to validate your contact.

evidence.proved: EU.org serves only the NS delegation; records live on the DNS host the delegation names
evidence.quote: To minimize administration, only domain delegation (NS records) is provided.

evidence.proved: the account and the domain request are made in the web application at nic.eu.org/arf/
evidence.quote: Create an account and request your domain here.

evidence.proved: the contact form asks for a name, an e-mail address and a postal address; name, e-mail, address lines 1 and 2 and country are required
the phone field carries no required attribute, so a phone number is optional

notes: The gate is a person, not a number: a manual validation with no published queue length or approval rate. That is a discretionary throttle, and a design that depends on it has no ceiling to plan against.
